newsitem.title: USA: Murphy Oil sets 97 capital budget $462 mln.
newsitem.headline: Murphy Oil sets 97 capital budget $462 mln.

text.p: Murphy Oil Corp said on Tuesday that it set the 1997 capital budget at $462 million, which is up four percent from projected capital expenditures in 1996.

Funds allocated to exploration and development activities total $402 million, or 87 percent of the total capital budget, while downstream capital expenditures are budgeted at $58 million. The remainder will be allocated to corporate activities, it said.
Murphy Oil said that expenditures in the U.S. account for $41 million or 18 percent of the 1997 development budget, while expenditures in the U.K. are budgeted at $79 million or 34 percent.

The development budget in Canada totals $96 million or 41 percent in 1997, and includes funds for Hibernia and a continuation of the program to develop the company's substantial heavy oil reserves by utilizing horizontal drilling/thermal production technology.
The continuing development of Block 16 in Ecuador accounts for the remainder, the company added.
